policy_decisions.guard_verified: Checked against local Postgres using JSON literals only. Results: non-empty array and non-empty object are true; [], {}, JSON null, the strings "555" and "", and the number 5 are false; a missing key, a string notifications and a missing notifications are NULL, which WHERE excludes. No input throws. Neither function can raise, so correctness does not depend on the order Postgres evaluates the AND.
policy_decisions.current_emitted_sql: Laravel 12 PostgresGrammar::compileJsonLength compiles whereJsonLength('settings->notifications->sms','>',0) to jsonb_array_length(("settings"->'notifications'->'sms')::jsonb) > ?. The cause is wrapJsonSelector plus str_replace('->>','->'). The column is jsonb (create_alert_settings migration :17), so the ::jsonb cast does nothing and the raw path settings->'notifications'->'<ch>' gives the same jsonb value.
policy_decisions.scalar_policy: A non-empty JSON scalar (e.g. "555") is NOT configured. The SQL excludes it, and the DTO normaliser maps any non-array value (null, '', scalar) to []. Reason: this keeps the stored shape, the form fill and the alert reader in agreement, so the UI never shows a recipient the reader won't alert. No writer in the repo produces scalars, and the prod error is the object variant (prep notes[0]).
policy_decisions.no_placeholder_char: The raw SQL contains no '?' (it is not the jsonb ? operator, and there are no bindings). The channel names are hardcoded literals from ['sms','emails','slack'], so nothing is interpolated from user input.

subtasks.title: Enforce the list-shape invariant on alert_settings channels: a no-throw reader guard plus writer/DTO normalisation
subtasks.approach: This is one coherent concern: channel values must be JSON lists, and the reader must survive when they are not. It stays one subtask because the reader guard, DTO normaliser and writer ->values() share one invariant and one test matrix. Splitting would mean duplicated fixtures and a DTO change that alters what the reader tests see. Five app files each get a small edit (about 40 lines in total). (1) HitAlertSettings::kitAlertSettings (app/Models/Concerns/HitAlertSettings.php:36-42): swap the three whereJsonLength/orWhereJsonLength calls for orWhereRaw(self::channelHasContentSql($ch)) over sms/emails/slack, using the guard in policy_decisions. Keep the orWhere('settings->webhook_url','!=','') branch, the cache key 'alert_settings:t:{type}:k:{kit}', the [10m,30m] TTL and the query shape exactly as they are. (2) AlertSettingSettingsDto (app/Dto/AlertSettingSettingsDto.php:19-42): add private static toList(mixed): array, which returns array_values for arrays and [] otherwise. Apply it to types, clients and the three channels in both fromArray and toJson. Guard a non-array 'notifications'. Leave webhook_url and the constructor unchanged. (3) AlertSetting::removeSms/removeEmail (app/Models/AlertSetting.php:122-136): add ->values() before ->toArray(). removeSms must read routeNotificationForSms() (human decision 2026-09-30). (4) AlertSettingsForm::formatSms/formatEmails/formatSlack (app/Filament/Forms/AlertSettingsForm.php:334-372): add ->values() before ->toArray(). (5) AlertSettingsCast::get (app/Casts/AlertSettingsCast.php:15): pass fromArray(is_array($decoded) ? $decoded : []) so a stored JSON null cannot TypeError. Leave set() alone; the array path is raw json_encode, and tests rely on it to seed bad shapes. Tests use the RefreshDatabase TestCase helpers (createUser(pro: true), makeOrgPro, factories). Seed malformed rows by creating them through AlertSetting::factory() and then overwriting the raw column with DB::table('alert_settings')->where('id',$id)->update(['settings' => '<literal json>']), because the DTO now normalises on write. Call Cache::flush() before each getSubscribers/notifySubscribers case and freezeTime() in the multi-case tests so the flexible window is deterministic. No ClickHouse is involved. Add sparse comments only, keep the code PHP 8.3-safe, and run composer format.

intended_diffs.diff: Inside the ->where(function (Builder $query): void { ... }) closure: foreach (['sms', 'emails', 'slack'] as $channel) { $query->orWhereRaw(self::channelHasContentSql($channel)); } then $query->orWhere('settings->webhook_url', '!=', ''). A leading 'or' inside a nested group is stripped by Grammar::removeLeadingBoolean. Add private static function channelHasContentSql(string $channel): string that returns "(jsonb_typeof({$path}) in ('array', 'object') and {$path} not in ('[]'::jsonb, '{}'::jsonb))" with $path = "settings->'notifications'->'{$channel}'". Add one short PHPDoc line: non-empty array or object counts as configured, and the expression never throws, unlike jsonb_array_length. The cache key, TTL and the whereIn/alertable_type/whereJsonContains(types) lines do not change.

fromArray: $notifications = \is_array($data['notifications'] ?? null) ? $data['notifications'] : []; then types: self::toList($data['types'] ?? null), clients: self::toList($data['clients'] ?? null), and notifications sms/emails/slack: self::toList($notifications['<ch>'] ?? null). webhook_url stays $data['webhook_url'] ?? ''. toJson: 'types' => self::toList($this->types), 'clients' => self::toList($this->clients), 'notifications' => ['sms' => self::toList($this->notifications['sms'] ?? null), 'emails' => ..., 'slack' => ...]. Add private static function toList(mixed $value): array { return \is_array($value) ? \array_values($value) : []; }.

In removeSms, change $this->routeNotificationForMail() to $this->routeNotificationForSms() and add ->values() before ->toArray(). In removeEmail, add ->values() before ->toArray(). Nothing else changes; routeNotificationFor*, alertsEmail/SmsIsSubscribedTo and the widget query are out of scope.
Add ->values() between ->unique() and ->toArray() in formatSms, formatEmails and formatSlack. save() does not change, because types and clients are normalised by the DTO.
In get(): $decoded = \json_decode($value ?? '{}', true); return AlertSettingSettingsDto::fromArray(\is_array($decoded) ? $decoded : []); set() does not change.

Use #[Group('alerts')]. Create one pro org (createUser(pro: true)) and add siblings with User::factory()->forOrg($org). Seed these rows. A: valid list (emails ['a@x.com'], types [L,S,M]). B: raw emails {"1":"b@x.com"}. C: raw sms "555" (scalar policy pin). D: raw slack null. E: raw emails {} and sms []. F: notifications key missing. G: webhook-only through the factory webhookNotification. H: valid emails plus raw sms "555". Use a #[DataProvider] over Hit::factory()->live()/stagingLive()/missedOpportunity()->forOrg($org). Assert getSubscribers() does not throw and its ids are exactly {A,B,G,H}. With Notification::fake() plus notifySubscribers(), assert b@x.com receives a notification, which pins AC-3. For H, assert routeNotificationForSms() is empty (scalar dropped). If the pipelines gate M differently, the M case falls back to asserting that kitAlertSettings resolution (via getSubscribers) does not throw.

removeEmail('b@x') on emails [a,b,c]: the raw column's jsonb_typeof(settings->'notifications'->'emails') is 'array' and the value is [a,c]. removeEmail on the first element also gives an array. After removeEmail, getSubscribers for a Live hit in the same org does not throw. removeSms('(555) 111-2222') on sms ['5551112222','5553334444'] with emails ['x@y'] leaves sms ['5553334444'] and emails unchanged (AC-5). A legacy raw object row {"0":"a","2":"c"} plus removeEmail('a') stores ['c'] as an array.

Add cases. fromArray with gapped or object-keyed types/clients/sms/emails/slack returns array_is_list values in the original order. For null, '', 'x' (scalar) and 5, the channel becomes []. A non-array 'notifications' makes all three channels []. toJson after direct mutation ($dto->notifications['emails'] = [1 => 'b']) emits a JSON list. The round trip is idempotent, and webhook_url is unchanged. The existing tests keep passing because they already use lists.

Add cases. get() with 'null', '"str"' and '5' returns a default DTO with no TypeError. set() with a DTO holding gapped arrays writes JSON arrays. The existing test_set_with_array raw path stays unchanged.

Add cases. The signed single-unsubscribe route removing the first or middle of [a,b,c] leaves the raw column jsonb_typeof 'array'. Unsubscribe-all after a prior removal still finds the row and removes the address.

Add cases. formatSms/formatEmails with a leading or middle duplicate, and with the personal entry toggled off where it is not last, return array_is_list results. formatSlack with an invalid URL at index 0 returns a list. save() persists the raw column with jsonb_typeof 'array' for all three channels. Use assertSame plus assertTrue(array_is_list(...)).

concerns: Reader: kitAlertSettings channel predicate must never throw and must count non-empty objects
Writers: DTO/cast/form/model persist and read channel, type and client lists as sequential arrays
sizing.why_single: Both concerns enforce one invariant and share one fixture and test matrix. The DTO read-path normalisation changes what the reader tests observe, so splitting would serialise anyway and duplicate the seeding. The total diff is small (about 40 app lines).

risks: The worktree has no vendor/ directory. Run composer install before the verifier runs tests (memory: worktree-vendor-missing-zod-migrations).

The DTO now also normalises on READ (cast get calls fromArray). A row whose sms is a non-empty scalar but that has another valid channel will now route SMS to nobody, where before it resolved to ['555']. This is intended per scalar_policy, and before this change such an org threw anyway.
HitEventListenerTest and HitWebhookFanOutTest are regression-only; the filter covers them and they are not edited.
Hit type M may be gated by the pipelines. If so, the M data-provider case asserts only that nothing throws, which keeps AC-1 coverage without a false negative.
